The Hyperparameters of a Fitted Model

Source: R/report.R
hyper.Rd

Reports every hyperparameter of every penalty that the model carries: one row each, with the value, whether it was held, and what put it there. A smoothing parameter, a prior scale, a lasso's \(\lambda\) and an elastic net's \(\alpha\) all appear here.

Usage

hyper(fit, scale = c("parameter", "link"))

Arguments

fit

A StatmodFit().

scale

"parameter" (the default) or "link". The argument is matched with match.arg().

Value

A data frame with one row per hyperparameter and the columns:

parameter

the distribution parameter whose equation contains the penalized term. For a covariance class that spans several equations, the names of all of them, separated by commas.

term

the term's key, its call as written.

name

the hyperparameter's own name, as the penalty names it.

estimate

its value, on the requested scale.

held

a logical: whether the term fixed it.

source

what produced the value, as above.

id

the sharing label, NA where the hyperparameter is not shared.

The result is a data frame of no rows, with those columns, where the model carries no penalty at all.

A hyperparameter is not a coefficient

It governs the coefficients under it instead of sitting beside them, and the two are estimated by different routes and reported with different qualifications. coef.StatmodFit() reports the coefficients, and this function reports the hyperparameters.

The two scales

scale = "parameter", the default, is the scale on which the penalty is written: a smoothing parameter is a positive number, and the sigma of a gaussian prior is a scale.

scale = "link" is the free scale on which the outer search runs, obtained through each hyperparameter's own link, and it is the scale on which the searches of two fits are compared. Where a hyperparameter carries no link, the two scales coincide.

The columns held and source

held is a logical that records whether a term fixed the value, directly or through the label that the hyperparameter shares. source records what produced the value:

  • "fixed" for a hyperparameter that a term holds, as in s(x, bspline_smooth(), hyper = c(lambda = 2)).

  • the name of the outer criterion ("reml", "ml", "aic" or "bic") for a hyperparameter that the outer search chose.

  • the name of the sparse criterion ("aic", "bic" or "cv") for a hyperparameter of a kinked penalty chosen along a path over its own values.

  • "" where no criterion ran, so that the value stayed at the starting value of its term.

The distinction matters for inference. A value chosen by aic(), bic() or cv(), whether by the outer search or along a path, is the argument of a minimum of a prediction-error criterion and not the root of the derivative of a likelihood, so the value does not yield a standard error. A value that reml() or ml() estimated carries a standard error, computed from the curvature of that criterion, and summary.StatmodFit() prints it.

Why two rows may carry the same number

Terms whose modelterms7::term_ids() give the same label estimate one value, and that value is written under each of their own keys. A shared hyperparameter therefore appears once per term, with the same estimate and the same source, and the id column marks the agreement as part of the model and not as a coincidence. The penalties are not merged, so each term still has a row of its own and the effective degrees of freedom are still counted term by term.

See also

coef.StatmodFit() for the coefficients, summary.StatmodFit() for the two printed together with standard errors, statmod_held() for which are held.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x = runif(80, 0, 1))
d$y <- sin(3 * d$x) + rnorm(80, 0, 0.3)

# The hyperparameter is estimated by REML, which the source column records.
fit <- statmod(y ~ s(x, bspline_smooth(k = 6)),
               distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), d)
hyper(fit)
#>   parameter                        term   name estimate  held source   id
#> 1        mu s(x, bspline_smooth(k = 6)) lambda 29.31279 FALSE   reml <NA>

# The same value is shown on the scale on which the outer search ran.
hyper(fit, scale = "link")
#>   parameter                        term   name estimate  held source   id
#> 1        mu s(x, bspline_smooth(k = 6)) lambda 3.378024 FALSE   reml <NA>

# Here the term holds the value instead, and it is reported as fixed.
held <- statmod(y ~ s(x, bspline_smooth(k = 6), hyper = c(lambda = 2)),
                distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), d)
hyper(held)[, c("name", "estimate", "held", "source")]
#>     name estimate held source
#> 1 lambda        2 TRUE  fixed
